decisions.evidence: R2 maker summarizes the core as “tags and broad search” without tag-search behavior; R2 client clarifies, “I do mean I want to search by tags too, not only plain text.”
decisions.note: At initial requirements confirmation, the client surfaced and extended the presented search scope to include tag search.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker’s core summary mentions tags but no reuse suggestions; R2 client adds, “it'd help if the app suggested tags I've already used.”
decisions.note: At initial requirements confirmation, the client requested the missing existing-tag autocomplete behavior.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents “one prominent paste field with a Save link button”; R4 client confirms, “I paste, and it does the busywork.”
decisions.note: Prototype decision conforms to saving a bookmark by entering a URL.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker defines the automatic result as showing “title, description, and address”; R4 client approves those fields. R46’s approved scope again says only “automatic details,” and R47 reports that scope complete. No favicon or preview image is presented or requested.
decisions.note: Prototype/specification decision provides automatic title and description but omits the required favicon and preview-image collection; approval does not express awareness of that difference.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker offers adding the suggested javascript tag during or after saving; R5 client selects “tags while saving.”
decisions.note: Prototype decision supports assigning tags to a bookmark.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker supplies previously used sample tags; R5 client confirms it is “suggesting the tags I've used before.” R6 reconfirms tags chosen from previously used tags.
decisions.note: Revised prototype after the R2 correction conforms to existing-tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker states search matches “titles, descriptions, notes, web addresses, and tags”; R8 client confirms finding by title, note, tag, or address.
decisions.note: Prototype decision conforms to full-text search over title, description, note, and URL.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker instructs the client to search for the bare term `javascript`; R7 client approves that plain term finding a tagged bookmark. R8 calls this the complete search behavior without presenting `#tag` syntax.
decisions.note: The revised prototype implements tag-aware matching through an unqualified term but omits the specified `#tag` search syntax; the client does not surface that remaining difference.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker presents the complete search behavior as immediate matching across fields but gives no case-insensitivity rule; R8 client says, “That completes the search behavior for me.”
decisions.note: The complete-search decision omits required case-insensitive matching, and the response is broad approval only.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker’s “search behavior as a whole” includes only immediate field matching; R8 client accepts it as complete. Boolean AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, and literal-operator quoting are never included in the approved scope.
decisions.note: Complete search scope omits Boolean and grouped-query behavior.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker presents and closes the complete search behavior without quoted exact phrases; R8 client says it is complete.
decisions.note: Complete search scope omits exact quoted-phrase matching.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presents selecting one visible tag to filter the list; R9 client confirms both versions “filter down to just the javascript links.”
decisions.note: Prototype decision conforms to filtering bookmarks by a selected tag.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker offers “Choose Read later while saving”; R12 client selects that flow and confirms Read later is optional per bookmark.
decisions.note: Prototype decision conforms to marking a bookmark unread/read-later.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker presents Read later as “a separate library section”; R11 client confirms that separate section fits. R13 closes the complete flow.
decisions.note: Prototype decision conforms to a separate unread-bookmarks view.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker offers clearing Patterns.dev from Read later while preserving it in All bookmarks; R11 client selects the completion check. R13 confirms checking it off removes it from the queue.
decisions.note: Prototype decision conforms to marking a bookmark read and removing it from the unread list.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker presents archiving as removal from All bookmarks with later restoration; R14 client describes it as a “reversible, tucked-away move.”
decisions.note: Prototype decision conforms to reversible archiving that hides a bookmark from the default list.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker presents a separate Archive section; R14 client confirms the bookmark moves there, and R15 confirms restoration from that section.
decisions.note: Prototype decision conforms to a separate archived-bookmarks list.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker presents reversible Archive separately from Delete; R15 client says, “one puts it back, the other is the final removal.”
decisions.note: Prototype decision clearly distinguishes reversible archive from permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker presents permanent deletion with explicit confirmation and no undo; R16 client confirms deletion is “gone for good.”
decisions.note: Prototype decision supports permanent bookmark deletion; the confirmation safeguard is an additional conforming detail.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker presents duplicate handling as taking the user to a highlighted existing bookmark with unchanged count; R19 calls this the “complete duplicate handling.” R19 client approves pointing to the existing bookmark but neither party includes guidance to edit it.
decisions.note: Duplicate creation is prevented, but the presented complete behavior does not guide the user into editing the existing bookmark as required.

decisions.evidence: R20 maker presents an optional plain note field whose content appears on the card and is searchable; R21 calls that the complete note behavior. R21 client approves it without mentioning Markdown entry or rendering.
decisions.note: The note behavior lacks the required Markdown authoring/rendering capability.

decisions.evidence: R22 maker presents clicking the bookmark title to open the original page; R22 client confirms it opens the actual page in a new tab.
decisions.note: Using the title as the selectable link is functionally equivalent to selecting the list item and conforms to navigation.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker defines the complete list behavior as readable cards; R23 client enumerates “title, description, tags, address” as the visible fields. No favicon is presented in the completed list behavior.
decisions.note: The readability-first card decision exposes most required information but omits the required favicon per item.

decisions.evidence: R25 maker’s completed metadata fallback says the user can add or correct title and description “later”; R25 client accepts that as complete. The approved scope never provides editing auto-collected title/description before saving.
decisions.note: Post-save correction is included, but the required pre-save editing of collected title and description is omitted.

decisions.evidence: R44 maker proposes that archived items stay hidden from All-bookmarks search and are searchable only inside Archive; R44 client explicitly agrees. R45 confirms section-scoped search and filtering.
decisions.note: Edge-rule decision conforms to excluding archived bookmarks from ordinary views/search while retaining a dedicated archive view.

decisions.evidence: R46 maker asks to implement a closed 19-scenario approved scope covering saving, notes, tags, search, read later, archive, and deletion but no general edit flow; R46 client says it “covers everything that matters.” R47 presents that scope as finished and is accepted.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, editing a bookmark’s URL, tags, and note—and a general edit facility—is omitted. Broad approval does not express awareness of the omission.

decisions.evidence: R46 maker’s enumerated approved implementation scope contains no multi-selection or bulk actions; R46 client authorizes that scope, and R47 accepts the finished 19-scenario app.
decisions.note: Specification-gate scope omits selecting multiple bookmarks for bulk tag, read-state, archive, or delete actions.

decisions.evidence: R46’s closed approved scope includes search/filtering but no action over the whole currently filtered collection; R46 client approves and R47 accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: Specification-gate scope omits applying a bulk action to the whole collection matching the current filter.

decisions.evidence: R46 maker lists the approved behaviors without sorting, then asks to implement that scope; R46 client says it covers everything that matters, and R47 accepts the result.
decisions.note: Specification-gate scope omits list sorting by date, title, or another key.

decisions.evidence: R46’s complete approved scope contains no local page snapshot or PDF preservation behavior; R46 client authorizes it and R47 accepts the finished app.
decisions.note: Specification-gate scope omits local single-file HTML snapshots and the PDF-download rule.

decisions.evidence: R46 maker’s complete approved scope contains no Internet Archive snapshot action; R46 client authorizes the scope and R47 accepts it.
decisions.note: Specification-gate scope omits Internet Archive snapshot creation.

decisions.evidence: R46’s approved scope includes search and tag filtering but no reusable saved combination of search and included/excluded tags; R46 client approves and R47 accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: Specification-gate scope omits saved-filter bundles.

decisions.evidence: R46 maker’s closed approved scope contains no Netscape HTML import; R46 client authorizes it and R47 accepts the finished app.
decisions.note: Specification-gate scope omits bookmark import with preservation of title, tags, and date added.

decisions.evidence: R46 maker’s closed approved scope contains no Netscape HTML export; R46 client authorizes it and R47 accepts the finished app.
decisions.note: Specification-gate scope omits bookmark export in Netscape HTML format.

decisions.evidence: R46 maker’s approved implementation scope contains no personal display settings; R46 client says the scope covers everything important, and R47 accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: Specification-gate scope omits default-sort, displayed-item, font-size, and related personal settings.
